title: Periodo ipotetico
intro: Sentences with *se* (if): the condition (*protasi*) and its result (*apodosi*). Each degree pairs its own tenses, in the colours used in the lessons.

head: Degree
Condition
Result
Examples
rows: Real or likely. The result can also be an order.
*Se {fs:finirò} presto, ti {fs:chiamerò}.* The future in both parts when both are in the future.
Possible but unlikely, or impossible now. The tenses are the same in both cases.
Possible: *Se {csi:vincessi} alla lotteria, {cop:comprerei} una casa al mare.*
Impossible now: *Se {csi:fossi} in te, non lo {cop:farei}.*
It did not happen, so neither did the result.
*Se {cst:fossi partito} prima, non {cpa:avrei perso} il treno.*

body: The *se* clause can come first or second: *{ip:Resto} a casa se {ip:piove}.* Never put the condizionale after *se*: not *se avrei*, but *se {csi:avessi}*.
A past condition can have a result now, and a lasting fact can explain a past result.

head: Condition
Result
Example
rows: *Se {cst:avessi preso} il treno, ora {cop:sarei} a casa.*

body: People often use the [im:imperfetto] in both parts of the 3rd degree: *Se lo {im:sapevo}, {im:venivo}.* It is fine in conversation, but write *Se l'{cst:avessi saputo}, {cpa:sarei venuto}.*
